sentences.text: You've saved 10 percent of a home's price.
sentences.spoken: You've saved ten percent of a home's price.

sentences.text: [curious] Do you buy now and pay mortgage insurance, or keep renting until you reach 20 percent?
sentences.spoken: [curious] Do you buy now and pay mortgage insurance, or keep renting until you reach twenty percent?

sentences.text: On the schedule alone, you can't even ask to cancel it for about 8 years.
sentences.spoken: On the schedule alone, you can't even ask to cancel it for about eight years.

sentences.text: We replayed real US prices and rates month by month, so you'll see how long it took on paper, typically and in slow cases.
sentences.spoken: We replayed real U.S. prices and rates month by month, so you'll see how long it took on paper, typically and in slow cases.

sentences.text: On paper means the loan is 80 percent of the home's value by a national price index.
sentences.spoken: On paper means the loan is eighty percent of the home's value by a national price index.

sentences.text: That's not the same as getting the insurance removed.
sentences.spoken: That's not the same as getting the insurance removed.

sentences.text: Removal on today's value, when you ask, is the loan owner's rule; for Fannie Mae loans, that's a waiting period and a 75 percent bar.
sentences.spoken: Removal on today's value, when you ask, is the loan owner's rule; for Fannie Mae loans, that's a waiting period and a seventy-five percent bar.

sentences.text: You'll also meet three illustrative buyers who got very different answers.
sentences.spoken: You'll also meet three illustrative buyers who got very different answers.

sentences.text: It's US only, history, not a forecast, and it won't say whether to buy or wait.
sentences.spoken: It's U.S. only, history, not a forecast, and it won't say whether to buy or wait.

sentences.text: Private mortgage insurance, or PMI, is a policy lenders usually require on a conventional loan with less than 20 percent down.
sentences.spoken: Private mortgage insurance, or PMI, is a policy lenders usually require on a conventional loan with less than twenty percent down.

sentences.text: It protects the lender if the loan goes bad, but the borrower pays for it, month after month, on top of the mortgage.
sentences.spoken: It protects the lender if the loan goes bad, but the borrower pays for it, month after month, on top of the mortgage.

sentences.text: What it costs depends on the loan and the borrower, so this video puts no dollar figure on it.
sentences.spoken: What it costs depends on the loan and the borrower, so this video puts no dollar figure on it.

sentences.text: What we can measure is how long it lasts.
sentences.spoken: What we can measure is how long it lasts.

sentences.text: So when does it end?
sentences.spoken: So when does it end?

sentences.text: Here's an illustrative example: a $400,000 home, a little under the national median price of new homes sold from April through June.
sentences.spoken: Here's an illustrative example: a four hundred thousand dollars home, a little under the national median price of new homes sold from April through June.

sentences.text: With 10 percent down, that leaves a $360,000 loan.
sentences.spoken: With ten percent down, that leaves a three hundred sixty thousand dollars loan.

sentences.text: At September's average mortgage rate, 6.86 percent, the monthly payment for principal and interest is the figure on screen.
sentences.spoken: At September's average mortgage rate, six point eight six percent, the monthly payment for principal and interest is the figure on screen.

sentences.text: Taxes, home insurance and the mortgage insurance all come on top of it.
sentences.spoken: Taxes, home insurance and the mortgage insurance all come on top of it.

sentences.text: Each payment pays the balance down a little, slowly at first, and faster later on.
sentences.spoken: Each payment pays the balance down a little, slowly at first, and faster later on.

sentences.text: By federal law, the borrower can ask to cancel the insurance once the schedule says the loan is down to 80 percent of the original value, here $320,000.
sentences.spoken: By federal law, the borrower can ask to cancel the insurance once the schedule says the loan is down to eighty percent of the original value, here three hundred twenty thousand dollars.

sentences.text: On this loan, that's payment 99, the date this video opened with.
sentences.spoken: On this loan, that's payment ninety-nine, the date this video opened with.

sentences.text: That request comes with conditions, such as being current on payments.
sentences.spoken: That request comes with conditions, such as being current on payments.

sentences.text: And the insurance has to end automatically when the schedule reaches 78 percent, as long as payments are current.
sentences.spoken: And the insurance has to end automatically when the schedule reaches seventy-eight percent, as long as payments are current.

sentences.text: Here, that's about 9.5 years in.
sentences.spoken: Here, that's about nine point five years in.

sentences.text: Both dates come from the schedule alone, and both ignore what the house is worth.
sentences.spoken: Both dates come from the schedule alone, and both ignore what the house is worth.

sentences.text: Lenders, and the investors who own loans, can also drop the insurance based on the home's current value.
sentences.spoken: Lenders, and the investors who own loans, can also drop the insurance based on the home's current value.

sentences.text: If prices rise, the same balance becomes a smaller share of the home, and 80 percent can arrive sooner, on paper.
sentences.spoken: If prices rise, the same balance becomes a smaller share of the home, and eighty percent can arrive sooner, on paper.

sentences.text: That's what on paper means in this video, and a lender's request, appraisal and minimum time still come after it.
sentences.spoken: That's what on paper means in this video, and a lender's request, appraisal and minimum time still come after it.

sentences.text: So how fast did rising prices actually get 10 percent down buyers there?
sentences.spoken: So how fast did rising prices actually get ten percent down buyers there?

sentences.text: We took every purchase month from January 1991 to July 2016.
sentences.spoken: We took every purchase month from January nineteen ninety-one to July twenty sixteen.

sentences.text: For each one, we set up the same 10 percent down loan at that month's average rate.
sentences.spoken: For each one, we set up the same ten percent down loan at that month's average rate.

sentences.text: And we let the home's value move exactly like the Federal Housing Finance Agency's national index of home purchase prices.
sentences.spoken: And we let the home's value move exactly like the Federal Housing Finance Agency's national index of home purchase prices.

sentences.text: Every month after that, we compare the balance with the value, and stop the clock the first time the loan is 80 percent or less.
sentences.spoken: Every month after that, we compare the balance with the value, and stop the clock the first time the loan is eighty percent or less.

sentences.text: Each bar here is one purchase month, and its height shows how long that took.
sentences.spoken: Each bar here is one purchase month, and its height shows how long that took.

sentences.text: The typical answer: 23 months.
sentences.spoken: The typical answer: twenty-three months.

sentences.text: Half of the purchase months got there sooner, and half took longer.
sentences.spoken: Half of the purchase months got there sooner, and half took longer.

sentences.text: And in 90.6 percent of them, prices got the loan to 80 percent on paper no later than the schedule would have.
sentences.spoken: And in ninety point six percent of them, prices got the loan to eighty percent on paper no later than the schedule would have.

sentences.text: That's the gap between the schedule's long road and the replay's typical one.
sentences.spoken: That's the gap between the schedule's long road and the replay's typical one.

sentences.text: But that's on paper.
sentences.spoken: But that's on paper.

sentences.text: We also checked a larger set: every purchase month since January 1991 with two years of prices after it.
sentences.spoken: We also checked a larger set: every purchase month since January nineteen ninety-one with two years of prices after it.

sentences.text: Two years after purchase, only 15.6 percent of them were at or below the 75 percent bar Fannie Mae sets for its loans when a borrower asks to cancel on today's value, a separate route from the law's schedule.
sentences.spoken: Two years after purchase, only fifteen point six percent of them were at or below the seventy-five percent bar Fannie Mae sets for its loans when a borrower asks to cancel on today's value, a separate route from the law's schedule.

sentences.text: So reaching 80 percent on paper in about two years was common in this history, while clearing that early bar by then was not.
sentences.spoken: So reaching eighty percent on paper in about two years was common in this history, while clearing that early bar by then was not.

sentences.text: The typical case also hides a long tail.
sentences.spoken: The typical case also hides a long tail.

sentences.text: About 1 in 7 purchase months took more than 5 years.
sentences.spoken: About one in seven purchase months took more than five years.

sentences.text: They sit together in one stretch of the grid, the months just before and during the national price slump.
sentences.spoken: They sit together in one stretch of the grid, the months just before and during the national price slump.

sentences.text: The slowest was October 2005: 112 months on paper.
sentences.spoken: The slowest was October two thousand five: one hundred twelve months on paper.

sentences.text: That's longer than the schedule itself took at that month's rate.
sentences.spoken: That's longer than the schedule itself took at that month's rate.

sentences.text: And this is a national average: no single home tracks it, and a local market can do much better or much worse.
sentences.spoken: And this is a national average: no single home tracks it, and a local market can do much better or much worse.

sentences.text: So why did the same rule give such different answers?
sentences.spoken: So why did the same rule give such different answers?

sentences.text: Three illustrative buyers, each with 10 percent down, show why.
sentences.spoken: Three illustrative buyers, each with ten percent down, show why.

sentences.text: Grace bought in June 2014, at 4.16 percent.
sentences.spoken: Grace bought in June twenty fourteen, at four point one six percent.

sentences.text: Her loan reached 80 percent on paper right at the middle of the replay: she is the typical case from before.
sentences.spoken: Her loan reached eighty percent on paper right at the middle of the replay: she is the typical case from before.

sentences.text: Her own schedule would have taken several years longer.
sentences.spoken: Her own schedule would have taken several years longer.

sentences.text: Owen bought in January 2004, while prices were climbing fast.
sentences.spoken: Owen bought in January two thousand four, while prices were climbing fast.

sentences.text: He reached 80 percent on paper in 13 months, the fastest in the replay.
sentences.spoken: He reached eighty percent on paper in thirteen months, the fastest in the replay.

sentences.text: Rising prices did most of that work, not his payments.
sentences.spoken: Rising prices did most of that work, not his payments.

sentences.text: [serious] Victor bought the year after Owen, in October 2005: the slowest month in the replay.
sentences.spoken: [serious] Victor bought the year after Owen, in October two thousand five: the slowest month in the replay.

sentences.text: Prices rose a little, then fell for years, and even when he finally reached 80 percent on paper, the index was still below where it started.
sentences.spoken: Prices rose a little, then fell for years, and even when he finally reached eighty percent on paper, the index was still below where it started.

sentences.text: He got there by paying the loan down, and his own schedule, at his lower rate of 6.07 percent, reached 80 percent of the original price first, at payment 90.
sentences.spoken: He got there by paying the loan down, and his own schedule, at his lower rate of six point zero seven percent, reached eighty percent of the original price first, at payment ninety.

sentences.text: Whether a lender would have dropped his insurance at that point, this data can't show.
sentences.spoken: Whether a lender would have dropped his insurance at that point, this data can't show.

sentences.text: Same rule, same national index: what differed was the month they started, and what prices did next.
sentences.spoken: Same rule, same national index: what differed was the month they started, and what prices did next.

sentences.text: So a plan can be measured against two benchmarks from this history.
sentences.spoken: So a plan can be measured against two benchmarks from this history.

sentences.text: One is the schedule the law uses, which on the example loan runs most of a decade.
sentences.spoken: One is the schedule the law uses, which on the example loan runs most of a decade.

sentences.text: The other is history on paper: a plan that counts on about two years matched the typical month, not the slow ones, and not the lender's step.
sentences.spoken: The other is history on paper: a plan that counts on about two years matched the typical month, not the slow ones, and not the lender's step.

sentences.text: On the illustrative $400,000 home, the other path, 20 percent down, means $40,000 more up front.
sentences.spoken: On the illustrative four hundred thousand dollars home, the other path, twenty percent down, means forty thousand dollars more up front.

sentences.text: This video doesn't weigh that against renting or waiting; it measures how long the insurance math took.
sentences.spoken: This video doesn't weigh that against renting or waiting; it measures how long the insurance math took.

sentences.text: How we know this, and what this video leaves out, is on this card and in the description.
sentences.spoken: How we know this, and what this video leaves out, is on this card and in the description.

sentences.text: [thoughtful] So how long does the insurance last?
sentences.spoken: [thoughtful] So how long does the insurance last?

sentences.text: On the schedule, the answer is set the day the loan starts; on paper, history gave answers from about a year to more than 9 years, and on paper is never the same as removed.
sentences.spoken: On the schedule, the answer is set the day the loan starts; on paper, history gave answers from about a year to more than nine years, and on paper is never the same as removed.

sentences.text: This is US only, and it's history, not a forecast.
sentences.spoken: This is U.S. only, and it's history, not a forecast.
